questions.question: What is a Callable in Java, and how does a Future give you its result?
questions.title: Java Callable and Future
questions.direct_answer: Callable<V> is a task that returns a value (V) and can throw a checked exception — unlike Runnable, which returns void and can't propagate checked exceptions. You submit a Callable to an ExecutorService, which returns a Future<V> — a handle representing the pending result. You call future.get() to block until the result is ready, cancel() to cancel the task, or isDone() to check without blocking. Callable is for tasks that compute a value (fetch a price, parse a file); Future is how you retrieve that value, possibly after waiting.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using Runnable where you need a return value, or calling future.get() immediately and blocking the caller unnecessarily.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Callable returns a value (V) and can throw checked exceptions (vs Runnable's void); submit to an ExecutorService to get a Future; get() blocks, isDone() checks, cancel() cancels.

sections.title: Callable Returns a Value; Future Retrieves It
sections.content: Callable<V> is an interface for a task that returns a value of type V and can throw checked exceptions — it's the value-returning counterpart to Runnable, whose run() returns void and can't propagate checked exceptions. You submit a Callable to an ExecutorService, which returns a Future<V>: a handle representing the pending result. The Future lets you call get() to block until the result is ready, get(timeout) to block with a deadline, cancel(true) to interrupt the task, or isDone()/isCancelled() to check without blocking. Callable is for tasks that compute a value — fetching a price, parsing a file, running a query — and Future is how you retrieve that value, often after waiting.

sections.title: From Callable to Result
sections.content:
A Callable is submitted to an ExecutorService, which returns a Future; calling get() blocks until the value is ready.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Callable<Integer>] -->|submit| E[ExecutorService]
  E -->|returns| F[Future<Integer>]
  F -->|get\(\)| R[Integer result]
  F -->|cancel\(true\)| X[cancelled]
```

sections.title: A Callable submitted and its result retrieved via Future
Callable vs Runnable and Future Methods
Common Mistakes
items: Calling future.get() immediately and blocking the caller thread, losing the concurrency benefit.
Using Runnable where a return value is needed — Runnable can't return one.
Not calling pool.shutdown(), leaking threads; or not handling get()'s checked exceptions.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Callable<V> returns a value and can throw checked exceptions; Runnable returns void and can't.
Submit a Callable to an ExecutorService to get a Future<V> handle to the pending result.
Future.get() blocks until the result is ready; get(timeout) blocks with a deadline.
Use isDone() to check without blocking; cancel(true) to interrupt a running task.
Don't call get() immediately if you can do other work — that defeats concurrency.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Callable is a task that returns a value and can throw checked exceptions, which is the key difference from Runnable, whose run method returns void and can't propagate checked exceptions. You submit a Callable to an ExecutorService, which returns a Future — a handle representing the pending result. The Future lets you call get to block until the result is ready, get with a timeout to block with a deadline, cancel true to interrupt the task, or isDone and isCancelled to check without blocking. Callable is for tasks that compute a value — fetching a price, parsing a file, running a query — and Future is how you retrieve that value, often after waiting. The common mistakes are calling get immediately and blocking the caller thread, which defeats the concurrency benefit, using Runnable where a return value is needed, and not calling pool dot shutdown, which leaks threads.
